newsitem.title: SWEDEN: SWEDISH SHARES FIRMER WITH FORESTRY SUPPORT.
newsitem.headline: SWEDISH SHARES FIRMER WITH FORESTRY SUPPORT.

text.p: Swedish shares remained firmer at midday Tuesday but off morning highs, boosted by a stronger forestry sector, stronger dollar and falling interest rates.
The general index rose 0.35 percent to 3,257.39 in fairly active turnover of 2.17 billion crowns.
The forestry sector was the strongest branch with the index up 2.13 percent after gains in New York overnight.

Swedish player AssiDoman rose five to 238 crowns after posting a six month profit after financial items of 859 million crowns against market expectations of 819 million crowns. Its profit a year ago was 1.23 billion crowns.

"It's slightly better than expected. But the market in general is very good and forestry companies in New York were up by more than two percent last night," Claes Vikbladh, forestry analyst at Nordiska Fondkommission, told Reuters.
The banking sector rose 0.94 percent amid continuing speculation and fuelled by news that Swedbank will take a 9.1 percent stake in HSB Bank which will start up in October.
Swedbank was four higher at 192 crowns.
S-E-Banken was 0.5 lower at 98 crowns ahead of releasing its half year earnings on Tuesday -- the first of the big four banks to report.
The market was expecting a profit after credit losses of 3.02 billion crowns compared to 2.72 billion crowns a year ago.

Other companies reporting six month earnings on Tuesday were speciality toolmaker Sandvik and tobacco products group Swedish Match . Sandvik was 5.5 crowns higher at 263 and Swedish Match edged up 0.70 to 24.90 crowns.

Market heavyweights Ericsson and Astra were weaker. Ericsson fell 2.5 to 364 and Astra lost two to 140 crowns. "Astra feels like dead money at the moment. I am recommending my clients reduce their holdings," said one broker. -- Stockholm newsroom +46-8-700 1017
